findings.title: The required unit check `pnpm test` fails under load: session-bound.test.tsx Y1c asserts an exact count of GET /me (2) that the product's own 2 s identity re-check window makes wall-clock dependent
findings.reproduction:
Candidate sha256:69b7412a… (source 3e3a06e), disposable clones $TMPDIR/rv and $TMPDIR/probe.

1. Run the full unit suite: `pnpm test --reporter=verbose`. On Node 22 and Node 24, with the other two round-5 reviews running (load average 13-17), it fails in 3 of 5 full runs. Each time the only product failure is apps/web/src/auth/session-bound.test.tsx › 'F-DG2-530/580 … (en) > Y1c: the same create under one identity still lands on the created record', at line 280: `expect(afterPost.filter(isMe)).toHaveLength(2)` receives 3. Logs: unit-node22.log (3895 ms), unit-node24.log (3276 ms), unit-node22-rerun.log (4263 ms). Because the root `test` script is `vitest run --project unit-node --project unit-web && vitest run --project unit-formula-nocodegen`, the failure also stops the formula no-codegen project from running in those runs. The same failure is disclosed in D-118 (BE-R5) and in the round-4 domain review (DOM-R4-02).
2. Deterministic reproduction (probes/sec-dg4-r5-y1c-timing.append.tsx, sha256 ebc53171…, appended to an unchanged copy of the spec in the probe clone only). It runs Y1c unchanged, except that one answer is held for 2.2 s once the POST is sent (the spec's own `hold`). Holding the answer of GET …/summary or GET …/audit gives the sequence 'POST | GET /me | GET /me | … | GET /me | GET /decisions…': a page GET sent more than SESSION_RECHECK_MS = 2000 (apps/web/src/api/client.ts:232) after the last /me revalidates /me first. That is the designed D-077 behaviour, but Y1c then sees 3 and fails. Holding the detail GET, the decisions GET or the /me answer gives 2 and passes (probe-Y1c-timing-node22.log).
3. The spec alone passes 6/6 (3 on Node 22, 3 on Node 24), and the full suite passes on both runtimes at load average 6-8 (unit-node24-rerun.log, unit-node22-rerun2.log).
findings.expected: A gate-required test is deterministic. Y1c bounds the /me count without depending on wall-clock timing, for example with controlled time (fake timers or the hold/release the spec already has), or by asserting the bound the design gives (the create's permission refresh, the navigation's identity confirmation, plus at most one revalidation per page GET sent after the 2 s window). Then `pnpm test` exits 0 whenever the product behaves as designed, whatever the machine load.
findings.actual: Y1c asserts exactly 2 /me requests after the POST. A third /me is correct product behaviour whenever any answer in the page load takes over 2 s, so the required `pnpm test` check exits 1 under load, without a product defect, in 3 of 5 full runs this round, and the formula no-codegen project does not run in those runs. Product security is not affected: the extra /me is the identity re-check working as designed, and every identity guarantee of the spec passes. Evidence only: the gate's required check is flaky, and each round has to explain it again.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG4 round 5 (T-DG4-REV-SEC-R5). Low, not mandatory: a test-determinism defect in a required check, with no product behaviour affected and a deterministic reproduction. It does not block the round.
